title: Verbal warning register - historical 2015-2016 practice
summary: A separate restricted workbook tracked lightweight verbal-warning/counseling events using employee, date, problem addressed and handler fields. The surviving entries are mainly cell-phone issues, with dress/customer-service examples, and the worksheet contains repeated embedded headers/irregular continuation rows.

claims.claim: The historical Verbal Warnings workbook uses four primary fields: Employee Name, Date, Problem Addressed, and Addressed By.

evidence.note: Employee names are excluded from generalized knowledge.

claims.claim: Eleven dated warning/counseling entries are recoverable in the supplied sheet between March 2015 and November 2016; eight are labeled Cell Phone Use, with the remainder covering dress code, a client complaint, and loud telephone behavior.
The workbook records who addressed the issue and shows more than one management/HR handler, indicating the register functioned as a cross-manager log rather than a single supervisor's notes.

The worksheet contains repeated copies of the header row and at least one irregular name-only/continuation row, demonstrating that the historical log was manually maintained and is not safe to parse as one header followed by uniform event rows.

The current 2025 handbook prohibits personal cell-phone use in the workplace and allows verbal counseling as the first Group A response for minor violations, providing current-policy context for the historical concentration of cell-phone verbal warnings without proving identical enforcement rules.

trigger: A supervisor/HR addresses a conduct or work-rule concern at the verbal/counseling level.
prerequisites: Identify applicable current policy and facts.
systems: Personnel file where separate documentation exists
steps: Address the issue with the employee.
Record the date, problem category and person(s) addressing it.
Link to separate counseling/warning documentation when one exists.
Escalate only under the applicable current discipline process.
decisions: Whether issue remains informal/verbal or requires a formal corrective-action record.
controls: Do not equate a register row with a complete disciplinary case record.
Row import must detect repeated headers and continuation rows.
Do not use historical issue frequencies to select current discipline.
unresolved_questions: Did this separate verbal-warning register continue after 2016, migrate into the annual disciplinary register, or move to another system?
What current system records informal verbal counseling so it can be found without duplicating the personnel file?
automation_candidates: Use a structured verbal-counseling log with stable event IDs and links to any formal personnel-file record.
Reject embedded header/continuation rows during legacy spreadsheet import.
Normalize issue labels while preserving the original source phrase.
